**Status: detailed implementation plan; targets are not wired.** This page
plans [`6_locate_clinics.R`][legacy-6]. It retains candidate coordinates,
identity evidence, spatial tests, and the selected-source label. A reported
point, an administrative center, and an inferred centroid are different
products and must remain distinguishable.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm Identities, Geometry, And Frozen Location Sources"}

Require `s2_clinic_ids_df`, `s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf`, and
`s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf` from pages [20](20_page-construct-clinic-ids.qmd)
and [23](23_page-construct-healthsheds.qmd). Use the in-memory spatial targets;
do not reread a shapefile export solely to reconstruct truncated field names.

Inventory and file-track the staged MDDSS, WHO, UNICEF, and separate GPS
sources, recording their source revision, coordinate fields, and CRS/axis
interpretation. Use frozen inputs rather than retrieving current master lists
from the web. The source labels its separate GPS coordinates as FKT centers;
do not relabel them as measured facility coordinates.

List the reviewed WHO UID replacements, ambiguous-source exclusions, and
GPS exclusions as explicit correction evidence. Minimum-name-distance matches
are candidate evidence, not independent proof of location accuracy.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Prepare Source Candidates Without Losing Provenance"}

| Proposed target | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `s6_clinic_location_sectorization_df` | Clinic attributes and parsed sectorization point coordinates |
| `s6_clinic_location_mdss_source_df` | MDDSS fields, excluding the source's zero/zero pair |
| `s6_clinic_location_other_sources_list` | Named WHO, UNICEF, and GPS source tables |

Preserve original identifiers and coordinate text alongside normalized numeric
fields. Distinguish empty strings, invalid text, and missing coordinates.
Do not exclude an individual zero coordinate just because the source excludes
the pair `(0, 0)`.

Place the source's `unique_nonNA()` behavior in a tracked helper or reuse an
equivalent already tested helper. Multiple nonmissing attribute values remain
an ambiguity to report. Do not silently pick the first. The unused legacy
`mode()` definition does not need a new target without an actual consumer.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Join MDDSS Through Historical Clinic Codes"}

Build `s6_clinic_location_mdss_joined_df` by matching character `FacilityID`
to the historical clinic-code crosswalk. Preserve the ASCII name
normalization and cosine-distance ranking. Keep equal minima and audit
multiple identities or candidate points instead of introducing a new cutoff.

The source has a commented-out distance threshold; it is not an active
scientific rule. Reproduce the subsequent clinic-name ranking after the join.
Record join expansion and unmatched codes so source multiplicity is visible.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Apply WHO Corrections And Add The Other Sources"}

Implement the exact WHO UID/name exceptions and reviewed duplicate choices
in `s6_clinic_location_who_clean_df`. Preserve removal of `#N/A` UIDs and the
trailing-minus coordinate repair, including which field controls the sign.
Add the WHO candidates with the legacy full join in
`s6_clinic_location_who_joined_df`, retaining clinics absent from sectorization.

Parse UNICEF's bracketed coordinate pair into
`s6_clinic_location_unicef_joined_df`. For
`s6_clinic_location_gps_joined_df`, preserve the two explicit exclusions, the
GESIS-to-ID candidate join, closest-name ranking, and distinct-row behavior.
Keep source coordinates separate rather than overwriting one generic pair.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Identify A Unique Matching FKT"}

Build `s6_clinic_location_fkt_matched_df` from sectorization candidates with
nonblank FKT names. Preserve clinic-name prefix removal, cosine distance,
name containment, and conversion of comma decimals and kilometer strings.

Reproduce the source's combined condition: minimum name distance, distance
`<= 0.12` or name containment, and minimum reported geographic distance;
a clinic with one candidate is treated separately. Retain an FKT match only
when exactly one candidate qualifies. Missing distances and ties need tests;
do not make an arbitrary winner to satisfy a uniqueness assertion.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Create Point Candidates And Containment Evidence"}

Create `s6_clinic_location_points_sf` with the five source point geometries
and their original coordinate columns in EPSG:4326. Missing coordinates must
produce the same empty-point semantics as the reference implementation.

Join healthshed and matched-FKT geometry to
`s6_clinic_location_containment_sf`. The legacy fields named `fktContains`
and `shedContains` actually use row-aligned `st_intersects()` results, not
strict polygon containment. Preserve boundary behavior and pairing by clinic
ID. Avoid a full candidate-by-all-polygons matrix when a row-paired operation
can reproduce it; verify equivalence before changing the implementation.

Containment success rates are diagnostics for the later check block. They do
not themselves select the preferred coordinates or establish measured accuracy.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Apply The Exact Source Precedence And Fallbacks"}

`s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf` will retain every candidate, the evidence,
and `which_use`, with the source's first-match ordering:

| Priority | Qualifying evidence | Label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–4 | WHO, sectorization, UNICEF, then MDDSS intersects the matched FKT | `who`, `sect`, `unicef`, `mdss` |
| 5 | GPS intersects the healthshed | `gps` |
| 6–10 | WHO, sectorization, UNICEF, MDDSS, then GPS intersects the healthshed | `who2`, `sect2`, `unicef2`, `mdss2`, `gps2` |
| 11 | Matched FKT geometry is nonempty | `fkt_centroid` |
| 12 | Healthshed geometry is nonempty | `shed_centroid` |
| 13 | No qualifying location | `none` |

The earlier GPS predicate makes the later identical GPS condition redundant
in the legacy order. Preserve and test that order before considering a
cleanup; do not claim all labels must occur in the data.

Keep the full selection evidence in an ordinary target, with any nonspatial
audit table persisted as a Parquet file target. Do not discard evidence in
order to produce only the selected coordinate pair.

:::

::: {.manual-procedure title="Define The Metadata Handoff And UNICEF Decision"}

[Page 25](25_page-combine-clinic-metadata.qmd) will consume
`s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf` directly. Keep `which_use` and the distinction
between FKT-based and healthshed-based selection even if a downstream display
label removes its trailing `2`.

The legacy metadata script lacks coordinate extraction cases for `unicef` and
`unicef2`, although this stage can select them. Record an explicit decision
between literal missing-coordinate parity and a reviewed extraction fix.
Do not change the source-selection order here to hide the missing case.
Selection can be implemented and checked before that downstream decision;
final coordinate acceptance depends on the recorded policy.

:::

::: {.manual-check title="Specify Location Acceptance Evidence"}

Create `tests/check-clinic-location-rules.R` before wiring the stage. Use
small synthetic candidate tables and polygons to test:

| Check | Required cases |
| --- | --- |
| Parsing | Empty and malformed coordinates, `(0, 0)`, bracketed UNICEF pairs, longitude/latitude order, comma distances, and WHO's sign repair |
| Identity | A code with multiple identities, equal name distances, full-join-only clinics, and unmatched historical codes |
| FKT choice | One candidate, equal minima, missing distances, name containment, and the `0.12` threshold boundary |
| Spatial evidence | Empty points, empty polygons, boundary intersections, row pairing, and deliberate overlaps |
| Source selection | Every reachable label, competing qualifying sources, no-coordinate fallback, and precedence of reported points versus centroids |
| Metadata contract | All emitted labels recognized by page 25 and UNICEF behavior matched to its explicit parity/correction decision |

After a separately authorized build, inspect candidate counts, unmatched IDs,
source-label frequencies, containment fractions with their denominators, and
unresolved ambiguities. Assert agreed key/cardinality contracts while keeping
exception records available for review. Do not treat a high intersection
fraction as validation of each individual coordinate.

```sh
python3 tests/check-manual-structure.py
```
